proposals.evidence: Turner’s section 3 *kṣaṭ/*kṣvaṭ gives Khowar c̣hoi, Bengali chay, Kumaoni chai, Western Pahari chɔ, Gujarati cha and Marathi sahā/sā. The selected forms belong to these named regional affricate or western sahā families, including ordinary source c/ts spelling, deaspiration and contracted h/v variants. They are kept separate from the northwestern ṣuvaṭ branch; added classifier material is excluded.

proposals.evidence: Full sapta gives the sāt/satt numeral throughout Indo-Aryan, including Old/modern Oriya sāta and western forms. These are simple seven responses with the source’s dental/retroflex and aspirated variants preserved; the Bhil hāṭ forms continue the corresponding s-to-h regional series. Forms containing a second eight numeral, a classifier, or a malformed bracket are excluded rather than reduced to seven.
